items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:12:1
items.html: This Nefesh is the discernment of the Gevurot, for in the Daat of the male there are Hassadim and Gevurot, since the firstborn takes a double portion: Know that the meaning of the five Hassadim of the Mochin is that the illumination of Hochma in them is in direct light, from above downward; and the meaning of the five Gevurot in the Mochin is that the illumination of Hochma in them is only from below upward, which is called reflected light, a female light, which is the light of the Nefesh. And remember this. And this is what he says, “Nefesh is the light of the Gevurot,” namely, only reflected light, as above. And he explains, “For the firstborn takes a double portion,” namely, ZA, which is called firstborn with respect to the Nukva, takes the five Hassadim and the five Gevurot in completeness, which are direct light and reflected light, as above; “and afterwards he gives the Nukva her portion, which is the Itra de Gevurot [crown of Gevurot],” for she cannot receive from him the illumination of Hochma in the discernment of direct light, called the Itra de Hassadim, but only in the discernment of reflected light alone, called the Itra de Gevurot, which is the discernment of the Nefesh, as above. And the reason of the matter will be explained in its place. And the reason the ARI calls ZA here by the name “firstborn” is that everything discussed here is in the discernment of the illumination of Hochma that distinguishes the male from the Nukva, as above. For this revelation applies only in the posterior vessels of ZA, that is, in his NHY from the Chazeh [chest] downward. And you already know that the posterior of the upper one is called “firstborn sons” with respect to every lower Partzuf, for the reason explained well above (page 739, the passage beginning “Firstborn sons”). And in order to hint to us precisely in which discernment he is speaking, he therefore calls him by the name “firstborn.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:12:2
items.html: Although, while she is still Achor be Achor [back to back] with ZA, her body is completed only through the Gevurot given to her from his posterior: He asks how we say here that in the first intercourse he makes in her the discernment of a vessel, whose meaning is the completion of the Gevurot, as above — while there he says that at the time the Nukva is still Achor be Achor, ZA completes her body in the discernments of the Gevurot, and then the Nukva is not yet fit for any coupling. It follows that he completes her Gevurot with no coupling at all, for a coupling and an intercourse are called only face to face, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:12:3
items.html:
Even so she does not take the Gevurot themselves, only their illumination, which passes through the Masach of the posterior of ZA: Meaning, there is a great difference between the Gevurot of Katnut and the Gevurot of Gadlut. For you know that the meaning of Gevurot is reflected light; but there is no reflected light except the discernment of the striking of the upper light upon the coarseness in the screen, as is known. Accordingly, there are two meanings in the word “Gevurot”: the first is the discernment of the screen and the coarseness in them; the second is the discernment of the reflected light that rises from them by the striking of the direct light upon the coarseness. And this is what the ARI distinguishes between the completion of the Gevurot that applies at the time of the Katnut of the Nukva, whose meaning is the completion of the screen and the coarseness received by her through the posterior and the screen of ZA, and the completion of this one — for this one certainly does not need a coupling, since the action of the coupling is the opposite action of this, for the coupling brings light and not coarseness. Therefore the ARI calls them “the illumination of the Gevurot” and not “the Gevurot themselves,” because the essence of the Gevurot means the reflected light in actuality, which is entirely light, since the reflected light is regarded as a part of the direct light itself, as is known. But the coarseness and the screen that she takes at the time of her Katnut are the discernment of the illumination of the Gevurot alone, and not their essence, as explained. And the reason he calls them by the name “illumination,” although they are only discernments of coarseness and screen, is that there is no influence from one Partzuf to another except by way of illumination: for the essence of the light that the Nukva receives from the hole in the posterior of the Chazeh of ZA — it is what builds the said coarseness and posterior, which is the secret of “And the Lord God built the rib,” as he wrote, that it will be explained in its place.
A note in the author’s own handwriting on the words “only their illumination, which passes through the Masach of the posterior of ZA”: It is the illumination that lowers the bottom Hey from the Einayim to the Peh, and draws the AHP, which is the secret of the Gevurot.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:12:4
items.html: The Gevurot themselves she takes only through a Zivug, etc.: Namely, in the secret of Mochin: he bestows upon her Mochin of the face from the coupling of the upper AB and SAG, which come to them through all the degrees, and they lower the bottom Hey from her Einayim to the Peh, and her AHP are found returned to her Rosh and to her interior. And then her posterior vessels — which are the discernment of her NHY, called Yesod and womb — and the lights that pertain to them are corrected. And then she is completed in the discernment of her Gevurot, in the discernment of their essence, for now she becomes fit to receive in them the MAN and the MAD [male waters], as above. For these completed Gevurot are the vessel that raises the MAN, and in them is the secret of the Ruach that her husband gives in her at the first intercourse, mentioned above.
